aspects.says: Application code never does PIN or key cryptography itself: it asks a security module through the SMAdapter interface, so a software (JCE) module and a hardware one are interchangeable and a test can stand in a mock.
The JCE security module is a software SMAdapter configured with a crypto provider and a local master key (LMK) file.
aspects.reason: configuration wiring that needs an LMK file; the exercise works against the SMAdapter interface instead

aspects.says: Keys are rotated on a schedule, and the previous key is kept for a while so transactions already in flight under it still verify.
aspects.reason: an operational policy built on a scheduler and a key store the page leaves undefined; nothing in it can be checked offline without inventing that store

aspects.says: A PIN travels only as a PIN block encrypted together with the card number from field 2, and the block goes into field 52 as its raw bytes; the clear PIN is never put in the message.
Messages between client and server travel over a TLS-protected channel.
aspects.reason: needs a live peer and sockets; a graded run is offline
